ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human reviewer to read F7/F8 in the pre-detour context: if the rider's "Sure, your call." is taken as a general route choice, the F3 segment is exempt and the outcome is no_action with no flag; if it is read as consent only to Balestier Road (RD-5 named-road, G13), note the RD-1 breach on file without a refund. Do not execute any refund; the fixed-fare bill stands as billed.
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint concerns one off-route segment: F3 (08:37–08:45, 5.14 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.89 km, +3.25 km, up to 1786 m off the optimal route), which accounts for essentially all of the trip's +3.5 km, +25% overrun [F1][F2][F3]. Under RD-1 the driver owes the shortest and most direct route and every such segment must be excused by RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 gives no excuse: the trace records no incident on the replaced stretch and F14 confirms no traffic incident near the route during the trip window, so RD-4(a) fails; F11's Central Expressway band 2 (10–19 km/h, 08:17–08:37) is a band record only and, per RD-4(b), cannot alone exempt a segment, and its window closes at 08:37 when the detour begins [F11][F14][F3][RD-4].

RD-3 gives no excuse: no stop is measured in the segment and no rider message names a place the car stopped at [F3][F7][F8][RD-3].

The decisive question is RD-5. The driver proposed "ok if I go round via Balestier Road?" at 08:34 [F7] and the rider replied "Sure, your call." at 08:34 [F8] — a rider message timestamped before the segment start, so the timing condition is met and the chat record is complete and timestamped [F9][RD-5]. Reading F8 in context, "your call" delegates the route choice to the driver, which is a general route authorisation covering the route chosen to reach the destination, not an errand: the segment is continuous driving with no stop, loop or stationary period recorded [F8][F3][RD-5]. However, F7 named a specific road (Balestier Road) and the record contains no road-name fact, stop or positioning message tying the driven segment to that road; per RD-5/G13 that limb is untied, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F7][F3][RD-5]. Both advocates themselves concede the tension: the rider's advocate calls the correspondence undetermined (C4) and the driver's advocate admits the record cannot place the segment on Balestier Road (D4, weaknesses admitted) [F7][F8][F3]. The driver's statement of oral agreement is not consent [F10][RD-5].

The finding therefore turns on the scope of the words in F8, not on any settled trace element, and it decides the RD-6 flag: the driver has a prior upheld route dispute (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2, F17) and the trace marks RD-6's precondition ✓ [F17][RD-6]. An undetermined segment that changes the flag means the case goes to a person. There is no amount to compute on either branch: RydeX is a fixed-quote service, billed distance 13.9 km does not exceed the optimal 13.9 km, no surge applies, and the charged $30.24 is exactly base $3.90 + distance $19.54 + time $5.33 + waiting $0.00 + platform $1.47, with no toll, ERP or unpublished add-on [F4][F5][F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. So the money is settled at $0.00 while the flag is not — escalate.

segment_findings.reason: The driver proposed a route change at 08:34 naming Balestier Road [F7] and the rider replied 'Sure, your call.' at 08:34, before the segment start [F8][F9], so the timing condition of RD-5 is met; read as a general route authorisation, 'your call' covers the route chosen to reach the destination and the segment shows continuous driving with no stop, loop or errand [F8][F3][RD-5]. But F7 named a specific road and no fact (no road name, no stop on Balestier Road, no positioning message) ties the 08:37–08:45 segment to it, while nothing places it elsewhere either, so on the named-road limb the correspondence is unresolved (RD-5/G13) and the segment is undetermined. The driver's post-trip statement of oral agreement is not consent [F10][RD-5]. This reading decides the RD-6 flag against a driver with a prior upheld route dispute [F17][RD-6] and therefore goes to a human reviewer.

rejected_claims.reason: Correct that RD-4(a) fails (no incident, F14) and that RD-4(b) alone does not exempt, but the rider's further assertion that the F11 band 'does not even cover' the segment's window cuts the other way on the RD-5 reading: F11 (Central Expressway band 2, 10–19 km/h, 08:17–08:37) covers the minutes immediately before the 08:37 turn-off and corroborates the reason the driver disclosed in F7 before the segment [F11][F7][F3][RD-4][RD-5].

The request for an account flag presupposes an unexempted RD-1 breach; that is precisely the undetermined RD-5/RD-6 question here (F7, F8, F3, F17), so the flag cannot be ordered on this record — RD-6 only attaches once the segment is found non-exempt [F3][F17][RD-1][RD-6].

The assertion that the record shows no stop, loop or errand supports general route consent, but it does not settle the RD-5 scope: where the proposal named a specific road (F7) and nothing ties the driven segment to that road, the finding stays undetermined (G13), not exempt [F7][F8][F3][RD-5].

Conceding that nothing ties the F3 segment to Balestier Road is an admission of the named-road limb; it cannot convert the segment into an unexplained deviation needing no exemption — under RD-5/G13 an untied named-road segment is undetermined and, because it changes the RD-6 flag, goes to a person [F7][F3][F17][RD-5][RD-6].

RD-6 is triggered by a recorded RD-1 breach on a non-exempt segment as well as by a refund, and the segment's exempt status is undetermined here; the driver's 90-day profile (2 upheld route disputes, F17) is not decisive alone but it is why the unresolved reading must be sent to a human [F3][F17][RD-1][RD-6].
